business_ops.seasonality: The routed text carries no dedicated seasonality section, but describes seasonal drivers within the supply chain and marketing discussion. Supply chain operations are stated to be designed to respond to seasonal availability, input-price movements and regional demand patterns while maintaining uninterrupted product supply. Procurement is typically aligned to harvest windows and harvest cycles, which the DRHP states supports consistency in product quality and enables sourcing across different phases of the commodity cycle; the DRHP notes that such procurement practices require higher inventory build-up during certain periods (the sentence is truncated at that point in the routed extract). On the demand side, brand ambassadors are engaged to increase brand awareness during seasonal bursts and new product launches, and a dedicated marketing team executes seasonal campaigns and localized retailer engagement. No quantified quarter-wise or month-wise seasonality of revenue is disclosed in the routed text.
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward linkage is via a direct, origin-linked procurement model rather than owned agricultural assets: raw materials are sourced from established suppliers across key spice-producing belts spanning Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan, supplemented by procurement through major trading hubs including Indore, Mumbai, Delhi, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Siliguri; procurement is typically aligned to harvest windows so as to source the right varietals and grades at the appropriate time for quality and pricing. Superior-quality hing is procured through international import channels via one of the Company's domestic suppliers. The DRHP states this model provides greater control over the quality, consistency and cost of raw materials and helps mitigate adulteration risks. Manufacturing is in-house at the two fully automated, ISO-certified facilities at Bardari and Bharosala in Indore, using vertical flow technology and automated process controls, with integrated cold-storage and warehousing infrastructure and in-house testing laboratories; packaging of soya and tea products is outsourced under job-work arrangements to Pragati Graphics Private Limited at its Rangwasa facility in Indore (Pragati Graphics and Packaging Private Limited also appears among the Fiscal 2025 top-10 suppliers). Forward integration runs through a Company-controlled route to market: logistics and warehousing infrastructure integrated with the Indore manufacturing operations, SAP-enabled logistics and inventory management systems, sales force automation and distributor management systems, an owned fleet of vehicles for transportation of finished goods to nearby locations and key logistics hubs (reducing dependence on third-party freight for last-mile delivery within core markets), a staged super-stockist-to-C&F distribution model for new states, and an owned direct-to-consumer online store, 'Pushp Online'. Supplier dependence has fallen over the period: purchases from the largest supplier were 17.34%, 16.08% and 6.49% of total purchases in Fiscals 2024, 2025 and 2026, and from the top 10 suppliers 55.12%, 51.36% and 45.72%.

overview.business_model: The Company manufactures, blends and packs spices at its Indore, Madhya Pradesh facilities and sells them in branded consumer packs across 24 states and union territories in India. Revenue comes from three product categories - pure spices (63.56% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026), blended spices (32.95%) and other products (3.49%, being soya products; tea products were launched in April 2026). Two brands address two price tiers: 'Pushp' for the premium category and 'Munimji' for the popular category. Blended and value-added products typically command higher product margins than pure spices. Sales are concentrated in Madhya Pradesh (67.45% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026), with Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand the next largest states.

genesis.founding_story: The business was founded in 1974 in Indore, Madhya Pradesh as a proprietorship named 'M/s Munimji & Sons' by Late Kishanlal Surana, when operations commenced from a small local outlet retailing spices under the 'Munimji Masale' brand. With the entry of the Promoters, Surendra Kumar Surana and Mahendra Kumar Surana, in the early 1990s, the business entered a phase of modernisation and expansion of operations, including the introduction of the 'Pushp' brand and a foray into blended spices and value-added categories. Over five decades it transitioned from a traditional player to a scaled, branded packaged spices business.

verdict.our_read: Pushp Brand (India) is a 1974-vintage Indore spices house that has finally scaled: FY26 revenue of ₹48,194.1 lakhs (+19.10% on FY25's ₹40,464.5 lakhs, itself only +1.61% on FY24's ₹39,824.3 lakhs, a two-year CAGR of 10.01% on my arithmetic) with PAT of ₹5,895.4 lakhs against ₹3,333.0 lakhs in FY24, net worth of ₹30,633.9 lakhs and total debt of just ₹1,937.1 lakhs (a fixed-deposit-backed overdraft, 0.063x debt to net worth on my arithmetic) and no contingent liabilities as at March 31, 2026. The operating improvement is real and not merely a treasury artefact: the DRHP's EBITDA margin of 12.32% to 15.92% to 17.16% is struck on total income, but stripping other income of ₹362.9 / ₹734.0 / ₹876.7 lakhs still leaves an operating EBITDA margin on revenue of 11.52% / 14.39% / 15.65%, a 413 bps expansion over two years (my arithmetic), corroborated by product margins the DRHP does print — blended spices 31.40% to 43.75%, pure spices 32.52% to 35.31% — and by FY26 production of 16,737 MT against 13,929 MT (+20.2%, my arithmetic), i.e. growth that was volume-led rather than price-led. Against that, almost everything structural points the other way. The franchise is one state — Madhya Pradesh is 67.45% of FY26 revenue and rising from 66.34% in FY24 even as the out-of-state distributor count went 642 to 752 — one category (pure spices 63.56%, with chilli alone ₹1,690.54 million of ₹4,819.41 million, 35.08% of revenue on my arithmetic) and one channel (general trade 95.14%, e-commerce and quick commerce 1.15%, against a packaged-food split the same DRHP's commissioned TKC report puts at roughly 76.0% general trade and 7.0% e-commerce in FY2025). Distributor concentration has genuinely eased (top-1 28.96% to 28.02% to 21.29%, top-10 52.65% to 50.42% to 43.83%) but the retention rate behind it collapsed from 99.47% to 70.69% to 72.44% while revenue per distributor stayed flat at ₹4.53 / ₹4.39 / ₹4.51 million — the network is being widened by churn and replacement, not deepened. Capital already committed is not working: owned installed capacity went 50,000 to 60,000 MT while utilisation barely moved, 35.38% to 37.14% to 37.19%, the DRHP simultaneously reports a 63,000 MT denominator that folds in a third-party job-work facility, and ₹5,685.2 lakhs — 85.6% of the ₹6,638.3 lakh step-up in net fixed assets on my arithmetic — went into an unused open plot purchased from the two promoters' own HUFs on a sale deed dated November 19, 2025, six months before filing, which is what lifted related-party transactions from 2.01% of revenue in FY25 to 13.59% in FY26. That purchase is also why FY26 cash conversion broke: CFO of ₹1,954.5 lakhs against PAT of ₹5,895.4 lakhs is 33.2%, and ₹8,639.6 lakhs of three-year CFO against ₹13,814.0 lakhs of three-year PAT is 62.5% (my arithmetic), with inventory up from ₹8,065.7 to ₹12,915.6 lakhs and the cash cycle out from 125 to 133 days. The record-keeping is the hardest single fact: a modification on maintenance of books of accounts recurs in the auditors' reports for FY24, FY25 and FY26 with no corrective adjustment made to the restated statements, and the specific matter includes the audit trail (edit log) not being enabled for changes made using privileged or administrative access at the database level — in a company whose FY24 comparatives were re-prepared as special purpose Ind AS statements only on May 18, 2026 pursuant to a SEBI letter, under an emphasis of matter restricting their use. The offer itself resolves the question of who this is for: a pure Offer for Sale of 7,445,000 shares in which the company receives nothing, with A91 Emerging Fund I selling 4,220,000 of its 5,663,460 shares (74.5% of its stake, 56.68% of the offer) and Sixth Sense India Opportunities III 1,545,000 of 2,196,040 (70.4%), while the two promoters part with 840,000 of 10,000,000 each (8.4%) at a weighted average cost of acquisition of ₹0.40 per share against A91's ₹159.50 and Sixth Sense's ₹460.04 — and the greenfield Indore facility phased from Fiscal 2028 has to be funded from internal accruals because no primary money arrives.

parameter_scores.basis: A brand pair dating to 1974 ('Pushp' premium, 'Munimji' popular), 312 SKUs, 1,016 distributors, over 368,000 retail touchpoints and 2,094 cities across 24 states and UTs, with new FY21-FY26 products at 12.01% of FY26 revenue. But no market share is quantified anywhere — the 'Pan-India player with leadership position in West and Central India' line in Basis for Offer Price has no supporting table — Madhya Pradesh is 67.45% of revenue and rising from 66.34% in FY24, distributor retention fell 99.47% to 70.69% to 72.44%, and revenue per distributor was flat at ₹4.53 / ₹4.39 / ₹4.51 million. Advertisement and sales promotion of ₹316.08 million is 7.69% of total expenses of ₹4,110.09 million.

Revenue ₹39,824.3 to ₹40,464.5 to ₹48,194.1 lakhs: +1.61% then +19.10%, a two-year CAGR of 10.01% (my arithmetic) against the category's own 12.6% CAGR for FY20-FY25 and 11.8% projected for FY25-FY30P. FY26 was volume-led (production 13,929 to 16,737 MT, +20.2%, my arithmetic) but FY25 saw production +5.00% on revenue +1.61%, so a full year of the record is realisation give-back. Scale remains small: total income ₹4,819.41 million against Orkla India ₹25,091.4 million and Tata Consumer ₹202,904.3 million (₹ million as printed in industry_peers.json), i.e. 19.2% and 2.4% respectively (my arithmetic).

Reported EBITDA margin 12.32% / 15.92% / 17.16% is struck on total income; on revenue and excluding other income of ₹362.9 / ₹734.0 / ₹876.7 lakhs the operating EBITDA margin is 11.52% / 14.39% / 15.65%, still +413 bps over two years (my arithmetic). PAT margin 8.29% / 11.13% / 12.01% on PAT of ₹3,333.0 / ₹4,585.6 / ₹5,895.4 lakhs. Corroborated by printed product margins: blended spices 31.40% to 43.75%, pure spices 32.52% to 35.31%. Finance cost is negligible at ₹142.1 lakhs and depreciation ₹344.1 lakhs. Held below 8 because a FY25 advertising cut of 21.7% (₹283.24 million to ₹221.79 million, my arithmetic) flatters part of the expansion, and the trajectory has not been tested against a full raw-material price upcycle inside the disclosed three-year window.

The FY24 base is a special purpose Ind AS restatement prepared on May 18, 2026 under an emphasis of matter restricting its use, so the three-year series is not three years of ordinary-course accounts. FY26 other income of ₹876.7 lakhs is 11.05% of restated PBT of ₹7,932.8 lakhs (₹793.28 million) on my arithmetic and is substantially treasury — profit on sale of investments and FVTPL fair-value gains, both added back in the restated cash flow statement. An FY26 exceptional loss of ₹37.1 lakhs (PBT before exceptionals ₹796.99 million reduced to ₹793.28 million) is referenced to note 35, which is absent from the extract, so its nature is unknown. A non-cash ESOP charge appears in FY26 against ₹3.28 million in FY25 and nil in FY24. Effective tax rate of 25.68% (my arithmetic) is unremarkable. Receivables over one year are ₹4.0 lakhs, and there were no product recalls or material contamination claims in the last three fiscals.

FY26 CFO of ₹1,954.5 lakhs on PAT of ₹5,895.4 lakhs is 33.2%; FY25 was ₹4,862.4 on ₹4,585.6 (106.0%) and FY24 ₹1,822.7 on ₹3,333.0 (54.7%); three-year CFO of ₹8,639.6 lakhs against PAT of ₹13,814.0 lakhs is 62.5% (all my arithmetic). FY26 CFO is 23.2% of EBITDA of ₹8,419.0 lakhs (my arithmetic). The driver is working capital: inventory ₹8,546.1 / ₹8,065.7 / ₹12,915.6 lakhs (42.2% of net worth, my arithmetic), inventory days 115 to 128, cash conversion cycle 125 to 133 days, against fast receivables at 18 days and payables at only 13 days. Reported cash is ₹19.9 lakhs, so liquidity sits in bank deposits and ₹263.33 million of current investments rather than in cash.

Net worth ₹30,633.9 lakhs against total debt of ₹1,937.1 lakhs — 0.063x on my arithmetic — and the borrowing is a fixed-deposit-backed overdraft facility. Contingent liabilities are a nil disclosure under Ind AS 37 as at March 31, 2026 (0.0% of net worth), no financing default in the last three fiscals, and receivables over one year are ₹4.0 lakhs. Marked down two points because cash is ₹19.9 lakhs with liquidity held in current investments of ₹263.33 million that include unsecured redeemable corporate bonds, InvIT units and AIF units carrying issuer credit risk; no credit rating has been obtained in three fiscals; and lender covenants require prior consent for changes in shareholding pattern, board composition and charter documents.

RoNW 16.78% / 18.75% / 19.24% against Tata Consumer 7.08% and Orkla India 10.39% for FY2026. Pre-tax return on capital employed of ₹32,571.0 lakhs (net worth ₹30,633.9 plus debt ₹1,937.1) on EBIT of ₹8,074.9 lakhs (EBITDA ₹8,419.0 less depreciation ₹344.1) is 24.8% (my arithmetic). The reading is muddied in both directions: net worth carries a large non-operating treasury book and an unused ₹5,685.2 lakh plot that depress the ratio, while other income of ₹876.7 lakhs sitting inside EBITDA inflates it. Utilisation of 37.19% means the operating asset base is producing this return at barely a third of nameplate.

Owned installed capacity went 50,000 / 50,000 / 60,000 MT while utilisation moved only 35.38% / 37.14% / 37.19%, and available capacity is 45,000 MT against actual production of 16,737 MT. The DRHP publishes two denominators — 63,000 MT including the third-party Rangwasa job-work facility, giving 38.95%, and 60,000 MT for the owned plants, giving 37.19%. Net fixed assets rose ₹5,074.4 to ₹11,712.7 lakhs, but ₹5,685.2 lakhs of that ₹6,638.3 lakh step-up (85.6%, my arithmetic) is an unused open plot bought from the promoters' HUFs, not productive capacity; CWIP is ₹72.0 lakhs. A further greenfield facility in Indore is proposed from Fiscal 2028 and, with no offer proceeds reaching the company, must come out of internal accruals. Capacity and utilisation rest on management assumptions (300 working days, 75% efficiency factor, 15 days downtime) certified by an independent chartered engineer, and the DRHP states they may not be comparable with peers.

parameter_scores.basis: Genuine de-risking on counterparty count — largest supplier 17.34% / 16.08% / 6.49%, top-5 41.70% / 38.80% / 28.41%, top-10 55.12% / 51.36% / 45.72% — with an origin-linked procurement model across MP, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan, in-house testing laboratories, integrated cold storage, SAP-enabled logistics and an owned delivery fleet. Offset by extreme single-origin dependence in FY26: 100% of kasuri methi from Rajasthan, 99.22% of turmeric from Maharashtra, 99.59% of laminates from Madhya Pradesh, 68.60% of coriander powder from Madhya Pradesh; hing with no domestic sourcing alternative, imported via one domestic supplier; procurement on purchase orders with no long-term agreements; and harvest-window purchasing that drove inventory to ₹12,915.6 lakhs at 128 days. Three statutory or regulatory proceedings and one criminal proceeding are pending against the company, quantified at only ₹0.20 million, but two go to product integrity: fipronil pesticide residues above the Regulation 2.9.3.2 limit rendering four packets of Pushp Tikha Tadka Teja Mirch 'unsafe food' under Section 3(1)(zz)(xii) of the FSS Act (complaint dated May 20, 2024, Chhota Udepur), and a Legal Metrology seizure of five packages of Munimji Turmeric Powder on November 8, 2023 with directors summoned on April 10, 2024 under Section 174 IPC; plus an Agar-Malwa charge sheet under Sections 52, 55 and 58 of the FSS Act. Against that: ISO 9001, ISO 22000 and HACCP certification, no product recalls or material contamination claims in three fiscals, and no material delays in obtaining or renewing approvals in three fiscals. But the Spices Board exporter registration has expired with renewal only applied for; 45 of 104 trademark applications are unregistered including 6 opposed and 2 refused (my arithmetic), with 8 marks expired; and statutory dues show small but repeated delays (ESI 26 days, TDS 46 days, professional tax 37 and 22 days, labour welfare fund 34 days).

The books-of-account modification recurs across all three restated years — auditors' reports dated September 30, 2024, September 25, 2025 and May 22, 2026 — with no corrective adjustment made in any of them, and the disclosed specific matter is that the accounting software's audit trail (edit log) was not enabled for certain changes made using privileged or administrative access rights at the database level. The FY24 comparatives exist only because SEBI required them, re-prepared as special purpose Ind AS statements on May 18, 2026 under an emphasis of matter restricting use. Group company financials for FY23-FY25 are kept off the document and hosted only on the company's website. A promoter declassified on November 26, 2025 after gifting 4,000,000 shares still drew ₹9.00 million remuneration plus ₹4.50 million of first-time professional charges in FY26; three promoter daughters draw ₹4.50 / ₹2.80 / ₹1.20 million as 'Assistant Directors'. All three independent directors were appointed between November 26, 2025 and March 2, 2026, the CFO on June 2, 2025, and only the IPO Committee is named. KMP post-employment benefits are not separately determinable. A 9:1 bonus within 18 months of filing completes the picture of a record assembled for the offer.

Systematix Corporate Services, one of three BRLMs, is confined to marketing activities only because its promoter and managing director Nikhil Khandelwal (2,136 CCPS, 0.08%), employee Rahul Khandelwal (632, 0.02%) and an employee's spouse Shikha Rajoria (634, 0.02%) hold securities beyond the Regulation 21C threshold. A recurring, unremediated inability to evidence that the ledger was not altered is the single most serious disclosure in this document, and it sits underneath every other figure cited here.

₹568.52 million (₹5,685.2 lakhs) paid to Mahendra Labhchand Surana HUF and Surendra Labhchand Surana HUF — the promoters as Kartas — for an unused open plot, on a sale deed dated November 19, 2025, six months before filing, equal to 85.6% of the ₹6,638.3 lakh net fixed asset step-up and 18.6% of FY26 net worth (my arithmetic), taking related-party transactions from 2.01% to 13.59% of revenue and simultaneously collapsing FY26 CFO to 33.2% of PAT.

FY24 comparatives exist only as special purpose Ind AS statements prepared on May 18, 2026 in response to a SEBI e-mail routed through the BRLMs on March 30, 2026, carrying an emphasis of matter that the statements may not be suitable for another purpose — so one third of the three-year track record is, by its own auditors' statement, not fit for the use to which the DRHP puts it.

Distributor retention fell 99.47% to 70.69% to 72.44% with no explanation, while revenue per distributor stayed flat at ₹4.53 / ₹4.39 / ₹4.51 million and onboarding more than doubled to 352 — the network's apparent growth to 1,016 distributors masks roughly three in ten leaving each year.

Two criminal food-safety and mislabelling matters are pending against a branded food company: fipronil pesticide residues above the permitted limit rendering Pushp Tikha Tadka Teja Mirch 'unsafe food' under Section 3(1)(zz)(xii) of the FSS Act, and a Legal Metrology seizure of Munimji Turmeric Powder with directors summoned. Quantified exposure is only ₹0.20 million, so the risk runs to brand and to director liability, not to the P&L.

The promoters' weighted average cost of acquisition is ₹0.40 per share against A91 at ₹159.50 and Sixth Sense at ₹460.04 — a 399x and 1,150x spread (my arithmetic) — built through a 9:1 bonus on February 19, 2025 and a nil-consideration gift of 4,000,000 shares in November 2025, in an offer where the company receives nothing.

Capacity utilisation of 37.19% is disclosed alongside a 38.95% figure on a 63,000 MT denominator that includes a facility the company does not own, while a further greenfield plant is planned from Fiscal 2028 with no primary proceeds to fund it — capacity is being added faster than it is being used and the funding is unstated.

One of three BRLMs, Systematix Corporate Services, is confined to marketing because its own managing director and employees hold securities in the issuer beyond the Regulation 21C threshold, while the board seats a nominee of the fund selling 56.68% of the offer — the syndicate and the selling side overlap the issuer at two separate points.

Every property the company operates from was acquired from or is leased from promoters, promoter group members or promoter-controlled group companies, and the financial statements of those three group companies are deliberately excluded from the DRHP and hosted only on the company's own website.
strengths_observed: Operating margin expansion is not an other-income effect: the DRHP's EBITDA margin (12.32% / 15.92% / 17.16%) is computed on total income, but removing other income of ₹362.9 / ₹734.0 / ₹876.7 lakhs still gives an operating EBITDA margin on revenue of 11.52% / 14.39% / 15.65% for FY24 / FY25 / FY26 — a 413 bps expansion over two years (my arithmetic). PAT margin moved 8.29% to 11.13% to 12.01%.

FY26 growth was volume-led: actual production at the two owned facilities went 13,266 to 13,929 to 16,737 MT, so FY26 volume rose 20.2% against revenue growth of 19.10% (my arithmetic) — unlike FY25, where production rose 5.00% against revenue growth of just 1.61% (my arithmetic), implying realisation gave way that year.

The mix shift is toward the higher-margin end the DRHP itself quantifies: blended spices product margin 31.40% to 39.22% to 43.75% against pure spices 32.52% to 33.68% to 35.31% and other products 26.48% to 25.26% to 25.98%; blended spices are 32.95% of FY26 revenue at ₹1,588.23 million.

Balance sheet carries almost no leverage: total debt ₹1,937.1 lakhs against net worth ₹30,633.9 lakhs (0.063x on my arithmetic), the borrowing is a fixed-deposit-backed overdraft, contingent liabilities are a nil disclosure as at March 31, 2026, there was no financing default in the last three fiscals, and receivables over one year are ₹4.0 lakhs (0.01% of net worth).

Supplier dependence has been materially reduced: largest supplier 17.34% to 16.08% to 6.49% of purchases and top-10 55.12% to 51.36% to 45.72% across FY24 / FY25 / FY26, with the FY26 largest supplier at ₹226.25 million of ₹1,593.06 million total purchases.

Working capital is collected fast at the customer end: trade receivable days 22 / 22 / 18, trade receivables ₹2,508.2 lakhs at FY26 on revenue of ₹48,194.1 lakhs, expected credit loss of ₹0.30 million in FY26, and the Madhya Pradesh core runs on credit of up to 40 days while other states run on advance payment.

Returns are ahead of the two listed peers the DRHP names: RoNW 16.78% to 18.75% to 19.24% against Tata Consumer Products 7.08% and Orkla India 10.39% for FY2026, notwithstanding that Pushp's total income of ₹4,819.41 million (₹ million as printed in industry_peers.json) is 19.2% of Orkla's ₹25,091.4 million and 2.4% of Tata's ₹202,904.3 million (my arithmetic).

Distribution reach widened fast in absolute terms: 853 to 1,016 distributors (stated 9.14% CAGR), retail touchpoints from over 237,000 to over 368,000, city coverage 1,021 to 1,498 to 2,094, 24 states and union territories, 103 modern trade stores, and 732 sales and channel management personnel as of March 31, 2026.

Portfolio breadth is being extended with measurable payback: 288 to 291 to 312 SKUs, products added between FY21 and FY26 contributed 12.01% of FY26 revenue from operations, and 4 new pure-spice plus 5 new blended lines were added in the 12 months before filing.
Employee attrition is improving off a very high base: 44.14% to 37.16% to 33.60% on a permanent headcount of 1,021 to 1,062 to 1,152, with nil KMP exits in each of the three years.

The category tailwind is documented: packaged spices grew from ₹206.6 bn to ₹374.3 bn at a 12.6% CAGR over FY20-FY25 and is projected at 11.8% to ₹653.4 bn by FY2030P, with branded spices carrying a stated 10% to 50% price premium over loose alternatives and blended spices described as mostly branded.

The materiality threshold ties out to the printed accounts: ₹23.02 million is stated as 5% of the average absolute PAT of the three restated years, and average PAT of ₹4,604.7 lakhs (₹460.47 million) at 5% is ₹23.02 million exactly (my arithmetic), so the litigation disclosure is anchored on a base consistent with the restated P&L.
